detectorPivotAffordable.question: Is running OLD detector over new code affordable (potentially 2× analysis during transition)?
detectorPivotAffordable.answer: UNMEASURED. The mechanism is correct and necessary to avoid false net-new regressions. Affordability is an engineering/product budget question, not settled by architecture. knownLimitations already states this. Dual-emit window exists precisely to keep detector0 runnable — good coupling.
detectorPivotAffordable.posture: Do not claim the pivot is cheap. Ship dual-emit only with a measured budget or an explicit product acceptance of 2× cost during major transitions. Prefer: pivot only when detector major changes and baseline compare is requested — not on every analysis.

A1_VER_05.question: Support windows all GUESSED — permanent?
A1_VER_05.answer: CONFIRM: marking NOT DISCHARGED is correct. VT-12 may be permanently unbuildable if grounding telemetry is refused by the threat model — that is honest tension, not paper. Product owner must either accept GUESSED windows as published policy (with label) or gather non-telemetry evidence (support ticket frequency, major adoption surveys).
A1_VER_05.note: Resolved-by-marking is the right architecture outcome when evidence is unavailable by design.

custodyPrinciple.question: Custody-keyed evolution policy?
custodyPrinciple.answer: Sound. USER-CUSTODY migrators, additive exit classes, refuse-don't-reshape, V7 reachability-follows-custody are the right set. run-manifest NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE residual is honest.

findings.title: Detector pivot cost unmeasured — dual-emit ship gate should require a budget disposition
findings.evidence: detectorSemanticDelta requires running detector0 over code1; knownLimitations: doubles work; no measurement; no conformance test bounds cost.
findings.impact: During multi-major support, every gate-compare may double analysis. Unbounded cost can make the correct classification unusable in CI time budgets, pressuring operators to skip pivot and reintroduce false regressions.
findings.requiredChange: Add a ship-gate note: dual-emit / pivot path requires product acceptance of cost bound OR an optimization (cache pivot results, pivot-only-on-detector-major-change). Do not leave affordability as silent assumption.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A measured fold on a reference repo showing pivot overhead within an accepted CI budget.

findings.title: Support windows remain GUESSED — property correctly NOT DISCHARGED
findings.evidence: dischargeStatus support windows NOT DISCHARGED; every evidenceGrade GUESSED; A1-VER-05 resolved by marking.
findings.impact: Published majorsSupported numbers look like promises. Without evidenceGrade surfaced to consumers, users treat guesses as SLAs.
findings.requiredChange: Any consumer-facing support matrix must display evidenceGrade or 'provisional'. Architecture already forbids sealing windows on GUESSED (VER-EG) — preserve.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Non-telemetry grounding method accepted by product and VT-12 made implementable.

findings.title: run-manifest migrator NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE leaves evidence bundles USER-CUSTODY without migration path
findings.evidence: knownLimitations; A1-VER-01 resolution excludes run-manifest from discharge lists.
findings.impact: Evidence bundle consumers can be stuck on a major with typed refusal only — correct under V3, painful operationally.
findings.requiredChange: Track as implementation backlog when evidence surface seals; not a versioning-policy text defect.

sealRecommendation.blocker: R1-VER-01: record cost disposition / ship-gate for pivot before treating dual-emit as ready-to-build without caveat. R1-VER-02 is already correctly marked — not a seal blocker for the *policy mechanism*.
sealRecommendation.afterChanges: Add pivot cost ship-gate note; keep support windows NOT DISCHARGED.
sealRecommendation.sealableNow: Three-way comparison classification, custody rules V1–V9, migrator *shape*, refuse-don't-reshape — these are independently sound (7/7 fixtures).
